items.excerpt: The internet was built for humans, not AI agents. Builder.io argues agentic traffic breaks today's web infrastructure and looks at how APIs like WebMCP may reshape how sites and products are designed.
A primer on Jev: what it is, how it compares to LLMs, what it costs, and how to wire it into product work for fast AI decisions, with a TypeScript demo.
Grok 4.7 is now available on Vercel's AI Gateway at 40% off through September 27, with a 500K token context window and selectable reasoning levels for prototypes built in v0 and fx.
A design proposal for 'AI nutrition facts' — an interface layer between writers, readers and AI that discloses how much of a piece was machine-generated.
UX Collective's weekly roundup on 'the death of the deliverable' — how AI is dissolving the artifacts designers hand off — plus a read on the iPhone Duo's UX.
Autodesk's own AI-made short film shipped with a continuity error no prompt could fix. VP of M&E strategy Maurice Patel explains why AI won't replace human animators.
A creative studio built 'CHAIMERA', a physical AI-slop monster sculpture, as a public promise never to ship generative slop. It debuts at the British Art Fair this week.
As AI video quality rises, 'AI slop' no longer describes what creatives are seeing. Creative Bloq argues the critique needs new vocabulary for competent-but-empty generated work.
An end-to-end workflow for shipping with coding agents: how to slice an epic, hand agents enough repo context, and get from issue to merged PR without losing review discipline.
A team red-teamed its own AI coding agent to stop 'scope escapes' — cases where the agent edits files and systems it was never asked to touch — and documents the guardrails that worked.
CG Channel's weekly roundup of CG tool updates, including animation library builder Animcraft, game engine Unigine, and OctaneRender.
NVIDIA lays out a layered safety approach for physical AI as robots and autonomous machines scale, with ABI projecting 49M L3-5 autonomous vehicles and ~60M industrial robots by 2035.
A practical guide to evaluating AI agents beyond single answers: measuring chains of sequential tool calls against a live environment and scoring real task completion.
From luxury watches to GPU cold plates, product teams are replacing slow solvers with AI surrogate models — and finding where the cost-benefit tradeoff actually holds up.
Snap says its Specs AR glasses, launching this fall, ship with a cross-platform AI agent and an optional cellular charging case — pushing agent UI onto the face.
Snap's CEO demoed the standalone true-AR Specs live on stage, including an official Harry Potter experience from HBO — a rare unedited look at spatial UI in the wild.
Acute Immersive lets businesses build custom immersive-video apps for Apple Vision Pro without a bespoke dev team, with publishing, monetization and analytics built in.
Daily AI use among marketers rose from 88% to 91%, yet fewer than half report better outcomes. The argument: advantage comes from redesigning the work, not adopting the tool.
Most company AI deployments can't learn from experience — every session starts from zero. The case for building memory into the AI your team works with every day.
When an embedded support agent issued an unauthorized action, nobody could trace the decision backward. A field guide to accountability and audit trails for agentic products.
AI got integrated faster than people could learn it. CompTIA's 2026 workforce study frames a skills-first training approach for teams facing a widening AI skills gap.
Google and five OEMs announced the first Googlebook laptops — Acer, Asus, Dell, HP and Lenovo — a new Gemini-first hardware class open for preorder today.
Designer Jesse Showalter puts Framer's agent to work fixing bugs in a live site build — a short, concrete look at agentic editing inside a mainstream design tool.
AI Jason pairs Jev with Treg to build fast automation workflows, showing where the new lightweight decision layer beats a full LLM call.
Matt Wolfe digs into a humanoid robot whose deliberately unsettling industrial design is doing real work — a look at how robot form language shapes user trust.
